questions.q: Arcadio Arellano is famously credited with the design of which humanitarian building in Manila, noted for its fine brickwork and Italian Renaissance-inspired details?
questions.n: Designed for the 'Proteccion de la Infancia,' this 1917 building is one of Arcadio's most beloved and preserved works.

questions.q: Which somber and grand structure in the North Cemetery did Arcadio Arellano design to honor those who fought for Philippine independence?
o: Mausoleum of the Veterans of the Revolution
questions.n: This massive, neo-classical structure is one of Arcadio's most significant civic contributions.

questions.q: Arcadio Arellano was the first Filipino to be employed as an architectural consultant for which government entity?
questions.n: He was appointed as the architectural consultant to the City of Manila during the early American period.

questions.q: The 'El 82' building, once a famous jewelry and hardware store in Binondo, was designed by Arcadio. Which stylistic influence did it famously showcase?
questions.n: Arcadio was a master at blending early 20th-century European trends like Art Nouveau with Filipino sensibilities.

questions.q: True or False: Arcadio Arellano was the father of the 'Arellano' architectural dynasty, but he passed away before he could see his brother Juan's greatest works completed.
questions.n: Arcadio died in 1920, just as the grand neoclassical era of the Bureau of Public Works was beginning its peak.

questions.q: Before becoming a professional architect, Arcadio Arellano was trained as a 'Maestro de Obra.' What does this traditional Spanish-era title mean?
questions.n: A Maestro de Obra was a master builder who handled both the design and construction management before the professionalization of architecture.

questions.q: Arcadio Arellano served as a captain in the engineering corps of the Revolutionary Army. Which president did he serve as an architectural consultant?
questions.n: Arcadio was an active supporter of the Philippine Revolution and provided technical expertise to Aguinaldo's government.

questions.q: The 'Gota de Leche' building is famous for its use of what specific material that gives it its distinct reddish hue and classic feel?
questions.n: The building is a rare and beautiful example of Italian Renaissance style translated through fine brickwork.

questions.q: Which of these residential houses, a transition between the 'Bahay-na-bato' and modern styles, is a notable work of Arcadio Arellano?
questions.n: Arcadio designed many residences for the elite, including the elegant Hidalgo house in Quiapo.

questions.q: In his works like 'El 82,' Arcadio integrated commercial spaces on the ground floor. This layout is a direct evolution of which traditional Filipino house part?
questions.n: In the Bahay-na-bato, the zaguan was the ground floor area used for storage and carriages, which easily transitioned into commercial use.

questions.q: Arcadio Arellano was often called the 'Architect of the Masses' during his early years. Why was this the case?
o: He lived in a humble bamboo hut despite his fame
He only built low-cost social housing
He refused to take payment for any of his work
His designs for charitable institutions like Gota de Leche served the poor
questions.n: His architectural contributions to public welfare and the revolutionary cause earned him great public respect.

questions.q: True or False: Arcadio Arellano was instrumental in the organization of the first professional body of architects in the Philippines.
questions.n: He was a key figure in the early efforts to professionalize the field, leading to the first licensing laws shortly after his death.

questions.q: The style of the 'Mausoleum of the Veterans of the Revolution' is largely neoclassical. What does this style symbolize in the context of a monument for heroes?
o: A total rejection of Western values
questions.n: The use of classical elements like columns and pediments was meant to give the fallen heroes a sense of eternal honor.

questions.q: How did Arcadio's career end compared to his younger brother Juan?
o: He became the Governor of Manila
He moved to Spain and never returned
He retired to become a full-time painter
He died relatively young at the age of 48
questions.n: Arcadio's death in 1920 cut short a career that was just beginning to fully integrate into the American-era boom.

questions.q: What is the shared architectural legacy of Arcadio and Juan Arellano often called in Philippine history?
questions.n: The two brothers, along with their descendants, formed the most influential architectural family in the early 20th century.
